title: perf(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need continuous detection of subtle latency and throughput regressions introduced by runtime, model, or kernel changes and automatic rollout guards to prevent bad variants from reaching production traffic. This PR adds an automated canary detector that computes rolling baseline distributions, triggers alerts when latency or throughput deviates beyond configurable statistical thresholds, and wires those signals into rollout guard policies used by the traffic manager.

What changed: Introduced a new perf-canary detector service (perf/canary/detector.go + detector config), expanded metrics (histogram buckets for p50/p95/p99 latency by model/route/instance), KV-aware checks that consider cache hit-rate impact on token latency, and adaptive hysteresis logic to avoid flapping. Added rollout guard integration (orchestrator/guards) so canary failures automatically stop/rollback rollouts and can trigger automatic narrow fallbacks to compatible model variants. New CLI toggles and console UI flags for canary sensitivity are included.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests and extensive synthetic canary tests added under perf/canary/test with injected regressions for latency and throughput. Bench harness run against prod-like traces (bench/harness/configs/canary-default). Staging canary run for two weeks without regressions on internal workloads. Feature is behind a feature-flag defaulting to enabled for redwood-managed canaries and disabled for customer-managed Dedicated clusters.

Backward compatibility and safety: This change is non-breaking; rollout guards default to conservative thresholds and require operator opt-in for automatic rollbacks in Dedicated. Metrics names are additive.

Follow-ups: Add ML-based anomaly detector to reduce false positives (ENG-2402), refine default thresholds per model family, and add a canary health dashboard drilldown (SRE-510).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice work. Two asks: 1) ensure metrics cardinality stays bounded by tagging only model_family+route, not full model version; 2) add a canary-mode dry-run that emits alerts but doesn't block rollouts so we can test sensitivity in prod.

Aisha Patel: Thanks — addressed both. Detector now collapses model version into family-level tag and added dry-run mode (config 'dry_run: true'). Updated tests and bench configs to cover dry-run behavior.
Sofia Martinez: Can we add a small cooldown after automatic rollback to avoid immediate re-rollouts? I'd prefer 5-15m default hysteresis.
Aisha Patel: Added configurable cooldown (hysteresis_ms) defaulting to 10m and a unit test to validate flare prevention.
Ben Carter: CI had one flaky bench test earlier but reran clean. Approving pending small doc note about Dedicated behavior.
Aisha Patel: Added short release note and console tooltip explaining Dedicated default off. Ready to merge.
release_notes: Add automated performance canary detection with KV-aware latency checks, adaptive hysteresis, and rollout guards. Feature-flagged; conservative defaults. CLI/UI toggles and new metrics.
